answer: Because the whisper index resolves every citation against the sable checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the opal audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 96 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 96 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 3 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
